item.title: MASM Operand Addressing: Distinguishing Memory vs. Immediate Values with Brackets
item.description:
“MASM Operand Addressing: Distinguishing Memory vs. Immediate Values with Brackets”

When programming with Microsoft Macro Assembler (MASM), the interpretation of operands, especially concerning memory access versus immediate values, can seem subtle, particularly when dealing with defined symbols and the use of square brackets ([]). How do you explicitly tell MASM whether you intend to access the address of a variable or the value stored at that address?

Symbol Definition and Implicit Dereferencing

MASM introduces typing for assembly symbols, unlike some other assemblers. If you define a symbol, say item, as a memory location of a specific type (like DWORD via DD), MASM infers your intent based on that definition.
